headline: Bengaluru Urban reports 5,828 moderately and 159 severely malnourished children, with over 30% stunting in city slums
summary: Bengaluru Urban district faces persistent child undernutrition despite being a tech hub. As of August 2021, 5,828 children were moderately malnourished and 159 severely malnourished. Studies reveal alarming rates: over 52% of slum children are stunted and over 30% underweight. A national survey found nearly 30% of under-5 children in the city were stunted, 26% acutely malnourished, and 28% underweight. Maternal anaemia remains a concern, with 35.6% of women anaemic, contributing to children being born undernourished.

reasons.detail: 35.6% of women in Bengaluru Urban are anaemic, contributing to undernourished newborns and poor maternal health outcomes.
In Bengaluru slums, over 52% of children under six are stunted and over 30% underweight, with 25% of households in poorest wealth quintile.
Studies in Austin Town and Anekal Taluk document inadequate dietary intake and suboptimal infant feeding practices among urban children.

modelFactorWhy.why: While maternal anaemia prevalence of 35.6% is documented for Bengaluru Urban, the pages do not specify iron-folic acid supplementation compliance rates or duration. The connection between maternal anaemia and child undernutrition is implied but not directly evidenced locally.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Adequate iron-folic acid intake during pregnancy prevents maternal anaemia, ensuring better foetal growth, higher birth weight, and reduced risk of stunting.
